questions.q: But-2-enal (CH₃CH=CHCHO) is heated with aluminium isopropoxide in propan-2-ol. The product is:
questions.explain: MPV reduction attacks only the C=O group, so the aldehyde becomes a primary alcohol and the C=C survives. Butan-1-ol would need the double bond reduced too.

questions.q: In the MPV reduction, the hydride that reduces the carbonyl carbon comes from:
options: The α-C–H of an isopropoxide group on aluminium
An Al–H bond of aluminium isopropoxide
questions.explain: The hydride moves from the α-carbon of an isopropoxide ligand to the carbonyl carbon through a six-membered cyclic transition state. No metal hydride or free hydride ion is involved, which is why only C=O is reduced.

questions.q: Why is acetone distilled out of the flask during an MPV reduction?
options: Acetone would reduce the product alcohol back to the carbonyl compound
Every step is reversible, and removing the lowest-boiling component pulls the equilibrium towards the alcohol
Acetone would undergo Cannizzaro reaction with the substrate
questions.explain: The reaction is an equilibrium; acetone (b.p. 56 °C) is removed as it forms so the alcohol is favoured. Running it the other way with excess acetone is the Oppenauer oxidation.

questions.q: An aldehyde with no α-hydrogen is subjected to MPV conditions. Besides the alcohol, the side product that may form is:
questions.explain: Aldehydes without α-hydrogen can undergo the Tishchenko reaction and give an ester. The aldol side reaction needs α-hydrogens, so it is the trap here.
